# @vignettes/theme-kit

The engine CSS layer that every [Vignettes](https://github.com/ShallowRed/vignettes) theme builds on. It is a set of SCSS files, and Sass is the one tool it needs.

A Vignettes theme sets colors, typography and sizes. This package provides what every theme shares: the semantic token contract, the Reveal.js patches, the slide skeleton, the media-layout grid, the spacing scale and the quicklink styles.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add -D @vignettes/theme-kit sass
```

## Use

```scss
// mytheme.scss
@use 'pkg:@vignettes/theme-kit';

:root {
  --accent: #e63946;
  --accent-soft: #fbdcdf;
  --accent-bg: #fef4f5;
  --surface: #ffffff;
  --surface-contrast: #1d1d1d;
  --on-contrast: #ffffff;
  --text-default: #1d1d1d;
  --text-title: #000000;
  --text-mention: #666666;
}

.reveal h1 { font-size: 3em; }
```

Compile it with Sass and its package importer, which resolves `pkg:`:

```js
import * as sass from 'sass'

const { css } = sass.compile('mytheme.scss', {
  importers: [new sass.NodePackageImporter()],
})
```

`pkg:` is [Sass's own package syntax](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/at-rules/use/#pkg) and needs Sass 1.71 or later. Inside a Vignettes application, `pnpm build:themes` does this for every theme it finds.

## The token contract

Code that works under any theme reads these custom properties only. A theme sets them, and this package ships defaults so a theme that omits one still renders.

- `--accent` is the primary color, for links, dividers and accents.
- `--accent-soft` is a lighter accent, for hover tints.
- `--accent-bg` is a very light tint, for callout backgrounds.
- `--accent-strong` is the accent mixed with the title color, for text on `--accent-soft` or `--accent-bg`, derived from `--accent` by default.
- `--accent-line` is the accent mixed with the surface, for the outlines of a diagram: the cards, the subject regions and the edge labels, derived from `--accent` by default.
- `--accent-on-contrast` is the accent mixed with white, for a mark on `--surface-contrast` or on a dark code block, derived from `--accent` by default.
- `--surface` is the page background.
- `--surface-contrast` is the inverse surface, for dark blocks and code panels.
- `--on-contrast` is the text color on `--surface-contrast`.
- `--text-default` colors the body text, `--text-title` the headings and strong text, `--text-mention` the muted text (captions, small print).
- `--border`, `--radius` and `--shadow` give the outline, the corners and the elevation of a box drawn by a component.
- `--code-min-size` is the smallest size of a code block, in slide units, `0px` by default.
- `--code-surface` and `--code-surface-dark` are the backgrounds of the code themes `clair` and `nuit`. By default they are the light and dark backgrounds of GitHub's code, `#f6f8fa` and `#24292e`, whatever the surface of the theme.

The kit derives three more tokens from the text intensities, at the root of the page: `--on-surface-title`, `--on-surface-default` and `--on-surface-mention`. A component that paints its own surface, such as a diagram card or a story frame, sets the text of that surface from them. A slide that changes its text colors, such as a dark section divider, leaves that surface with its dark text.

## The card palette

`color="green"` on a node or a region of a diagram (`@vignettes/schemas`) reads three properties: `--palette-green-text` for the title and the icon of the node or the region, `--palette-green-bg` for the surface of a region and `--palette-green-main` for its outline. The kit defines `blue`, `green`, `yellow`, `orange`, `brown`, `pink`, `purple` and `grey`. A theme redefines these properties, and adds names of its own with the same three properties. A name the theme leaves undefined takes the accent tokens.

## What it contains

`_semantic-tokens.scss` declares the contract above, `_palette.scss` the card palette. `_reveal-patches.scss` adapts Reveal.js defaults and bridges MDC's wrapper elements with `display: contents`. `_slide-structure.scss` is the flex skeleton of the three slide kinds the engine tags on each section: `slide-h1` for a title slide, `slide-h2` for a section divider, `slide-h3` for a heading with body. It aligns the content of a slide vertically, as `:layout{align}` asks or by the default of the slide kind and of its layout, and reads two size tokens a theme sets on `.reveal`: `--slide-heading-min-height`, the height a content slide keeps for its heading, and `--slide-body-padding-y`, the space above and below its body. `_media-layouts.scss` is the grid behind the media layouts. `_spacing.scss` and `_quicklinks.scss` cover the spacing scale and the in-deck navigation links.

## The base skin

```scss
@use 'pkg:@vignettes/theme-kit/base';
```

Applies the nine color tokens to the page background, the text, the headings, the links, inline code, quotes, list markers and the navigation controls, with a system font. With the layout preset, a theme can consist of the tokens alone: [examples/themes](https://github.com/ShallowRed/vignettes/tree/main/examples/themes) holds a dark theme and a brand theme written that way. A theme that draws these elements itself leaves the base skin out.

## The layout preset

```scss
@use 'pkg:@vignettes/theme-kit/presets/layout';
```

Gives a theme the type scale and the spacing of the French state design system, and leaves the colors to the theme. Use it to keep those proportions under your own palette; [@vignettes/theme-dsfr](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@vignettes/theme-dsfr) is the full theme.
